records.context_summary: Describe how line and belt transects are used to sample organisms and assess biodiversity in an area.
creditworthy_points: Seven marking points are listed, 4 marks available: transect is systematic not random sampling; straight chosen line across the habitat; sampling along the whole line or at set points; line laid with rope/string/tape (line transect); only organisms touching the line counted; quadrats placed along the line (belt transect); all organisms of each species in the quadrat counted.
examiner_findings: [misconception] Candidates do not understand how transects collect data; they treat a transect as random sampling although the area is deliberately chosen along a line (report p.40). (report p.40)
[misconception] Candidates use 'transect' and 'quadrat' as synonyms (report p.40). (report p.40)
[language/terminology] Some wrote rectangular blocks/columns/bars for quadrats, and 'quadrants' for quadrats (report p.40). (report p.40)
[omission] Candidates did not say that organisms of each species are counted (not calculated or measured), nor that a key is used to identify species (report p.40). (report p.40)
common_errors: Calling a transect random sampling.
Treating transects and quadrats as the same thing.
Describing measuring or calculating organisms instead of counting them.
strong_response_features: Distinguish line transect (only organisms touching the line) from belt transect (quadrats along the line, all organisms counted) and say species are counted and identified with a key.
notes: mapping_method: by meaning; confidence: high
stem: "Describe how transects are used to assess the biodiversity of an area."

Paper 2 held as 8223-2.pdf (unlabelled); tariffs reconcile with printed question totals. Table 1.1 antelope data accompanies the question but part (a) is method recall. Max-4 of 7 points inferred from tariff; the report does not print a 'max' line for this part.
